summary: Iteration 222 — Functional assessment of the three-portal suite (AI KARAU, ENZI, MedMatch AI). Backend smoke test (10/10 passed) covering admin auth, karau-meet meeting CRUD + LiveKit token, generic /api/livekit/token, /api/livekit/status, ENZI /api/lumi/channels, observability errors list+stats. Frontend: portal selector renders all 3 cards with 3 Open buttons; admin login at /login succeeds and stores access_token; MedMatch /resume, /agents, /meeting-notes all load with proper headings and no critical JS errors; KARAU /webinars renders the WebinarPage with full webinar list (live + scheduled) and 'New Webinar' button; KARAU /karau-meet landing renders correctly; ENZI /lumi loads its own 'Sign in to ENZI' page (separate ENZI auth — by design); /admin/errors loads the Error Logs page showing 3 unresolved errors with full traces (observability working end-to-end).

minor.issue: Returns object {meetings:[...]} not a bare list — confirm OpenAPI matches; not a defect, just shape note.
Body schema requires `room_name` (not `room`); 422 if wrong field — documented.

ui_bugs.issue: React warning: 'Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop.' in render method of WebinarPage. Missing key on mapped webinar list items.

/karau-meet/webinars and /karau-meet/webinar/{id}/live fall back to the KARAU landing hero ('Meet. Connect. Collaborate.') instead of rendering the webinar list or the LiveKit live room. The top-level /webinars route works, so this is a sub-route wiring gap inside KarauMeetPortal.

Console error 'Failed to load Google APIs: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading load)' from Google Identity Services bootstrapping. Page still renders fine — cosmetic SDK init race.

integration_issues.flow: Webinar host speaker queue (raise hand → host queue → Promote next)
integration_issues.issue: Could not exercise live UI in the test env: the WebinarHostControls + RaiseHandButton components are mounted inside LiveKitRoom only after a successful LiveKit cloud connection. /karau-meet/webinar/{id}/live did not enter the room (sub-route fell back to landing — see UI bug above). Static review confirms: WebinarHostControls.jsx uses useParticipants/useDataChannel('handqueue','handcontrol'), maintains ordered handOrder map, exposes a Promote-next via /api/karau-meet/meetings/{id}/participants/{identity}/role; RaiseHandButton broadcasts handcontrol data channel events. Backend /participants/{identity}/role endpoint is wired (host-only, calls LiveKit UpdateParticipant). End-to-end LIVE verification of the queue advance requires a real LiveKit room with two participants and is blocked by the routing fallback above.

issues: Some cards (e.g., 'Distance Zero: Next-Gen Communication') extend description text past the card border; consider line-clamp-2 for the description.

action_items: Fix React 'key' prop warning in WebinarPage's webinar list .map() — add a stable id key.
Wire /karau-meet/webinars and /karau-meet/webinar/{id}/live sub-routes inside KarauMeetPortal so they render the WebinarPage / MeetingRoomSwitch instead of falling back to the KARAU landing page.

Verify that /api/karau-meet/meetings/{id}/livekit-token issues a host token when the caller is the meeting owner (today's test created a meeting and then requested a token successfully — confirm in product that is_host flag is set so WebinarHostControls actually mounts).
Optional: harden the Google Identity Services bootstrap on /resume to avoid the 'Cannot read load of undefined' console error.
critical_code_review_comments: LiveKitMeetingRoom only renders WebinarHostControls when both `webinar` prop and `isHost` are true; ensure the parent (MeetingRoomSwitch) passes webinar=true for webinar-type meetings — otherwise the speaker-queue feature is invisible even to hosts.
WebinarHostControls uses useDataChannel('handqueue','handcontrol') reliably=true — good. handOrder is a useRef map keyed by identity which preserves FIFO across re-renders. Good.
/api/karau-meet/meetings/{meeting_id}/participants/{identity}/role uses async LiveKit UpdateParticipant and properly catches TwirpError 'not_found' — good defensive coding.
Observability page already filters out _id correctly (page renders cleanly) — good MongoDB hygiene.
Frontend admin layout reads admin@medmatch.com from auth/me and renders the dashboard correctly; token stored as 'access_token' in localStorage — consistent with backend response.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% — all primary portal flows reachable; 1 sub-route fallback issue and 1 React key warning

seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_iter222_meeting via /api/karau-meet/meetings during backend test (left in DB, non-blocking; admin-owned).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/test_iteration222_portals.py as regression. The speaker-queue LIVE verification still needs a real LiveKit-connected webinar room with 2 sessions (host + attendee) — the test env can issue tokens but the /karau-meet/webinar/{id}/live sub-route currently falls back to the KARAU landing page, so the LiveKitRoom never mounts in-app. After main agent fixes the sub-route wiring (KarauMeetPortal Routes), re-test: (1) navigate as admin to /karau-meet/webinar/<a real webinar id>/live (2) confirm [data-testid=livekit-meeting-room] mounts (3) open a second incognito session as a non-host attendee and click RaiseHandButton (4) verify host sees the entry in the queue panel and 'Promote next' POSTs to /api/karau-meet/meetings/{id}/participants/{identity}/role.
rca of the issue: The /karau-meet/webinar/{id}/live route falls back to landing because the inner <Routes> tree in KarauMeetPortal.jsx (line 31 imports MeetingRoomSwitch and line 343 returns it) is gated by location-based conditionals that aren't matching the URL pattern shape, so the default landing renders. The top-level /webinars route renders WebinarPage correctly (proving the page itself works), confirming the regression is inside KarauMeetPortal's path-matching, not in MeetingRoomSwitch or LiveKitMeetingRoom.
